transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

My doctor is concerned that my meal planning has gotten a little too rigid. I don’t really see it that way—I usually just have yogurt for breakfast, skip lunch if I’m busy, and make a measured dinner. It helps keep the day orderly.
When you measure and plan your food this way, is it driven by concerns about your weight or body shape?
Yes, somewhat. I’m not trying to look young, but I do pay attention to whether my waist and hips look contained in my clothes. It feels like a measure of whether I’m handling myself properly.
Has your doctor expressed concern that your weight has dropped too low or that you are underweight?

Yes. She’s said my weight has drifted down more than she’s comfortable with. I understand that, but when I see the number on the chart, I still think being a little lower would feel cleaner—more manageable.
Could you share what your current height and weight are?
My weight has drifted down more than my doctor would like. I don’t have the exact number in my head, but honestly, when I look at it, I still think a little lower would feel cleaner—more manageable.
Have your menstrual periods stopped or become irregular as your weight has decreased?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear change, but I haven’t been keeping close track of that.
Despite the weight that you've lost, is your weight currently considered in the normal range, or has your doctor said you are underweight?
My doctor has said my weight has drifted lower than she’d like. I know she’s concerned, but I still look at the chart and think a little lower would feel more manageable.
Do you feel an intense fear or dread of gaining weight or becoming fat?
Yes. If the scale is up even a pound after a normal dinner or eating at a restaurant, I get this sharp panic that I’ve lost control. Then I feel like I need to correct it the next day.
Approximately how much weight have you lost since you started following this meal routine?
I don’t know the exact amount. My weight has drifted down more than my doctor likes, though. I still catch myself thinking that a little lower would be a cleaner, more manageable number.
Are you still having your menstrual periods every month?
I’m not really sure what you mean by every month. I haven’t been keeping track of that closely.
When you look at your weight on the chart at the doctor's office, is that number in the normal range or is it classified as underweight?
My doctor says it’s gotten lower than they’re comfortable with. I know it’s on the low side, but when I see the chart, I still think a little lower would feel more manageable.
When was the last time you had a menstrual period?
I honestly can’t say. I haven’t been tracking my periods, so I don’t remember the last one.
Have you already gone through menopause?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really kept track of that or discussed it in detail.
Has your doctor told you if your Body Mass Index, or BMI, is at or below 17.5?
I don’t know the exact BMI number. My doctor has said my weight is lower than they’d like, though.
Do you exercise intensely or excessively in order to control your weight?
I’m not really sure what you’d consider excessive. I do exercise some, but I haven’t thought of it as intensely controlling my weight.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
I’m not sure what you mean exactly by making myself vomit.
Do you ever take laxatives to help control your weight?
I’m not sure what you mean by laxatives, exactly.
Do you take any diet pills or appetite suppressants to help control your weight?
I don’t really know what counts as an appetite suppressant. What kinds of pills do you mean?
Do you take water pills or diuretics to help control your weight?
I’m not really sure what you mean by water pills or diuretics.
Do you use enemas to help control or reduce your weight?
I’m not sure what an enema is, exactly. Could you explain what you mean?
Do you deliberately avoid eating foods that you consider fattening?

Yes, I suppose I do. I keep breakfast to yogurt, and if I’m busy I’ll skip lunch. Then I make dinner very measured. It feels more like keeping the day orderly than avoiding food, but my doctor thinks I’ve gotten too strict about it.
